_comment: Per-row disposition for every preflight advisory pinned in example_fidelity_snapshot.json (#737 item 1). The snapshot pins WHAT each audited example emits; this file says WHY each of those rows is there, so the gate is a zero-UNEXPLAINED-advisory bar rather than a drift pin. Entries are keyed by (variant, code) and carry the number of pinned rows that pair covers -- rows that share a code on one variant are the same condition on different ports, axes or entities, and the snapshot already pins each one's full text. test_example_fidelity_contract.py asserts the mapping is a bijection and that the row counts add up, so a new advisory, a removed one, or a stale entry all fail. disposition: 'intended' = the example deliberately shows or tolerates this condition (reason cites the example's own docstring/comment or the physics); 'defect-open' = the example should not emit this and the fix needs work beyond this file's PR, with the issue number that tracks it. A defect small enough to fix leaves no entry -- the row is gone from the snapshot instead. validation/crossval/* scripts belong to the crossval leader session (#928): their rows are classified here, never edited.

entries.reason: This variant exists to SHOW the advisory. The tutorial reads TE101 three ways (yee, ADI at factor 2, ADI at factor 5) and prints the frequency error each way 'so the accuracy-vs-timestep trade is visible rather than asserted'; its own docstring says the default factor 5 'carries a visible wavelength-scale error (shown below)'. run_and_read() prints the report verbatim and labels it 'quoted verbatim, not suppressed'.

The demo never time-steps: its docstring is 'Create a shareable rfx artifact bundle (scene + mesh + report) WITHOUT running FDTD', and main() only calls export_artifact_bundle(). The advisory is about excitation coupling during a solve (a single-cell port in substrate cannot drive the patch TM mode, issue #71); this scene has no patch and no solve, and the advisory itself is part of what the exported review report carries. No number this example prints depends on the port.

make_sim() is the shared EMPTY domain factory -- 'Build the small open domain shared by every material example'. The script always follows it with add_sample(), which adds the source and probe. The advisory therefore describes the half-built simulation this build-only gate audits, not anything the example runs: the six end-to-end solves in main() all go through add_sample() first. It is a statement about the audited entry point, not about the example's physics.

The tutorial models FR4 with sigma=0 on purpose and says so at the build: 'FR4 is modelled lossless (sigma=0) so preflight's infinite-Q advisory will fire: legitimate here -- we quote mode FREQUENCIES, not absolute Q (real FR4 tan_delta ~0.02 would cap Q near ~50).' It reports frequencies, never a Q, so the advisory names a modelling choice the example has already justified.

The example's subject IS the graded mesh: its own Rule 2 states 'NU TRADES ACCURACY FOR CELLS', and the z profile is built by ceil() onto a graded spine, so a design edge that does not land on a node is the trade the tutorial is demonstrating. The build prints the realized PEC sheet planes next to the declaration, which is the disclosure this advisory asks for.

The builder draws its conductor sheets without regard to where a PEC sheet's edge is solved, and this mesh realizes them off their drawn size: thin_conductor[1] 'thin_conductor[1]' x: drawn 29.5mm, nodes cover 28mm, solved as 28.7mm (-2.71%); thin_conductor[0] 'thin_conductor[0]' y: drawn 55mm, nodes cover 55mm, solved as 55.7mm (+1.27%); thin_conductor[0] 'thin_conductor[0]' x: drawn 60mm, nodes cover 60mm, solved as 60.7mm (+1.17%). A sheet end strictly inside the domain is solved about 0.35 cell beyond its last PEC node (measured, scripts/diagnostics/pec_sheet_edge_offset.py), so the worst row here -- thin_conductor[1] 'thin_conductor[1]' x: drawn 29.5mm, nodes cover 28mm, solved as 28.7mm (-2.71%) -- is what build_simulation actually solves, not a rounding note. Nothing in the script compensates for it; the mesh-side remedy (rfx.mesh_edges.edge_aware_profiles) postdates the script. Left as drawn here: changing a published or gated model's mesh is its owner's decision, tracked on the rasterization issue.

Teaching point 3 of the tutorial: 'Every face should sit at least half a wavelength from the radiator where the domain allows. The face below the ground plane cannot: it sits 6 mm below the ground. Preflight flags it, the run quotes the warning verbatim, and a solver-to-solver cross-check backs the placement. Preflight output is part of the result; do not suppress it.' The placement is cross-checked against openEMS at the design-mode bin (|D_rfx - D_openEMS| = 0.0659 dB).

The geometry is the openEMS 'Simple Patch Antenna' tutorial verbatim -- a 60 x 60 mm finite ground plane -- and the finite plane is the structure under test, not an oversight. main()'s comment lists this row among the advisories expected on this fixture: 'the small-ground-plane pattern advisory (60 mm = 0.56 lambda at f_max, so edge diffraction shapes the pattern) -- expected physics, shared with the openEMS reference, not a solver defect'.

Same reason, stated in the same comment: 'the off-lattice conductor-face residual on the patch and ground outlines (1 mm on a 2 mm cell). Measured 2026-09-07: four advisories, and both of the last two fire.' The patch (32 x 40 mm) and ground (60 x 60 mm) are the published openEMS dimensions and dx = 2 mm is 'coarse on purpose' with a measured 22-minute runtime; re-cutting either to the lattice would stop the fixture from being the reference geometry its +3.5 % / -0.07 dB comparison is built on.

The slab Box is drawn (-1 m, -1 m) to (1 m, 1 m) transversally ON PURPOSE and the code says why: 'The material Box must span the full transverse extent (incl. CPML padding): with TFSF the transverse axes are periodic, so any cell outside the material mask breaks the plane-wave assumption (detail (c)).' The advisory measures the declared face at -1 m, which is an over-draw that the domain clips, not material sitting in the absorber by accident.

Docstring: 'Preflight will flag the under-resolution and the lossless slab -- both are expected here: this is a fast method demo, we measure R/T (not Q), and a lossless slab is what matches the lossless analytic Fresnel reference.' The advisory's own text carves this out ('Harmless if you are not measuring Q').

Same docstring sentence: the grid 'is kept coarse for speed; halving dx reduces the error toward the analytic curve', and the under-resolution is named as expected. Three rows = the three axes of the one dielectric.

The 2 mm gap the advisory measures is the fixture's defining dimension: two PEC bars at z = 5 mm and z = 7 mm with the driven wire port in between, and the build-time check asserts exactly those wall planes ([3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9] mm). The decision quantity is rho(f) = v/i at the driven cell against a known external load, which is a circuit-law measurement on that gap, not a propagation measurement that needs cells per wavelength.

The variant IS the NU arm: 'POST = NU lane, uniform-valued dz_profile, run()' is one of the two arms the experiment compares, so dz_profile is set by construction. The advisory reports an rfx limitation (the shared wire-port primitive covers the uniform path only, issue #544), not a property of this fixture, and the fixture answers it directly: RC.assert_wall_planes checks the realized live/dead terminals the advisory asks the reader to inspect.

Every row is a deliberate feature of the FIX-A falsifier fixture. The 'short' load is four 1-cell PEC columns bridging the 1 mm gap between two electrode plates ('pec' x/y-extent 500 um = 1.0 cells), and the gap rows (1000 um = 2 cells along z, 500 um = 1 cell along x/y, and the 0-cell gaps where the columns touch the plates) are the terminals the experiment measures rho(f) across. The pre-declaration binds this geometry; the build asserts the realized wall planes rather than trusting a thickness convention.

The four one-cell PEC volumes named by the advisory ARE the shorting columns of the 'short' load. 'Realized as a filled slab with walls on BOTH faces' is what a short across the gap has to be, and the script's own comment makes that the point: 'a volume realizes walls at BOTH its faces and shorts every normal edge between them at ANY thickness, so the gap faces at z = 3.5 mm and z = 4.5 mm are terminals by construction'.

Same as issue683: the battery is declared 'NU lane only (POST-injection ordering, measured correct per #683)' and runs with an explicit dz_profile, so the uniform-only dead-cell classifier (#544) cannot speak. The fixture replaces it with an explicit build-time terminal assertion.

FIX-T is the canonical two-port THRU battery fixture, verbatim: a microstrip trace over a z_lo PEC ground (boundary z=Boundary(lo='pec', hi='cpml')). Infinite ground + finite trace is the microstrip model. The harness prints every preflight row verbatim per arm (preflight_verbatim()).

The substrate is declared lossless because both frozen records are: the openEMS tutorial and the Palace run solve eps_r 3.66 with no tan_delta, and this arm is compared with them. The arm quotes a notch FREQUENCY and an |S21| magnitude, never a Q, and it carries the case's own ring-down witness (-40 dB) to show the record ended after the lossless stub stopped ringing.

This arm's subject is exactly that residual. A PEC sheet's in-plane edge is solved about 0.35 of a cell beyond its last node, so the offset arm puts the node 0.35 of a fine cell INSIDE the metal and draws the sheet at its true 600 um: the declared face then sits 16.54 um (0.35 x 47.24 um) off the nearest node BY CONSTRUCTION, which is what this row reports, and the metal's solved edge lands on the drawn one. The instrument's R3 refuses any build where that distance is not the offset the arm declares, and the build test's mutation (c) shows the refusal firing.

The board IS a microstrip: its ground is the z_lo PEC face and its line and stub are finite PEC sheets on the substrate top, which is the configuration this advisory describes. The crossval case this arm extends declares the same boundary (BoundarySpec z lo='pec') and both external records -- openEMS's own MSL_NotchFilter tutorial and the Palace FEM run -- are taken on an infinite ground plane, so a finite one would be the wrong board, not a safer one.

The study IS a mesh-refinement study: 'Arms: multiband P-C at s in {1, 1.5, 2, 3}; uniform-fine control at the same scales; reference = uniform-fine at s=2/3.' The audited variant is the s = 1.5 arm, so a coarse-cell advisory on the substrate (10.7 cells/lambda_eff) and the superstrate (15.0, exactly at the bar) is the arm doing its job -- supraconvergence is measured BY running under-resolved arms against a fine reference. Silencing it would delete the observable.

This variant exists to be REJECTED: the script is 'intentionally conservative' and demonstrates that 'a centered homogeneous dielectric cavity is rejected by production validation with precise fail-closed reasons'. The advisory reads 'dielectric on x: 12.5 cells per lambda_eff ... Need >=15'; the coarse mesh is the case under test, and no observable is claimed from this arm.

The uniform arm deliberately reuses the rejected case's mesh so the two are comparable: it 'is solved on the uniform reference lane and checked against the analytic TM110 resonance, proving that the material setup is physically meaningful even though that centered subgrid case is [rejected]'. Its claim is checked against a closed form, which is what makes 12.5 cells/lambda_eff acceptable to state.

The finite reflector is the structure: 'An x-oriented electric dipole (Ex point source) sits a quarter wavelength above a finite PEC reflector plate'. The advisory says the pattern will carry ground-plane edge diffraction, which is exactly what a 0.83-lambda plate does and what the steering objective optimizes against. (It reads 0.83 lambda since the lattice snap in this PR; it read 0.90 lambda from the DECLARED bbox before, while the plate this lane actually realized was 0.75 lambda.)

The demo's observable is the |S21|^2 notch of a shunt open stub as a function of stub LENGTH, optimized by jax.grad; the references it is scored against (the analytic quarter-wave stub length, the brute-force L scan on the same lossless board) are lossless. A dielectric loss tangent would move the notch DEPTH, which the demo reports as a design output of its own cost surface and not against any measured board.

The 2 normal intervals the advisory counts are the declared mesh: DX = 127e-6 with the comment 'h_sub / 2 -- 2 substrate cells. Demo geometry of record. Refining to 80 um (cv06b standard) gives a cleaner eps_eff staircase but exposes a dx-fragility in the plane lane (|S21|^2 > 1 unphysical) that is a follow-up; for now the demo runs at h_sub/2 where the extractor is well behaved.' One row per MSL port.

Disclosed in the source with the arithmetic that makes it unavoidable: 'The residual +5.8% width error is NOT fixable by redrawing: W_TRACE / DX = 4.72 is not an integer, and gcd(254 um, 600 um) = 2 um, so no sane uniform dx puts both the substrate top and both trace edges on node lines. That is disclosed here, not absorbed.' The substrate face, which the port checks key off, IS on a node (H_SUB / DX = 2 exactly).
Microstrip model again: the board's ground is the z_lo PEC face and the through-line trace plus the stub are the finite PEC sheets.

The 0.5 mm cell is the fixture, not a choice this script is free to make: the number it measures is the published central-difference slope of the SAME board at the SAME mesh, and refining the cell would compare a different antenna against it. The coarse-mesh staircase offset is what the published ladder already quantified; this script measures the DERIVATIVE at that mesh, and its own convergence witnesses are the h ladder and the 2x record, not a finer cell.

The deformation IS the experiment: eight cells inside the patch's +x node line stretch and the eight just outside shrink, and those eight end four cells short of the x_hi absorber runway, so the grading reaches it by construction. The window is the published one, kept so the slope is comparable; the end-of-run energy witness the script records (-116 dB of peak at the record used, -122 dB at twice it) is what says the absorber is not returning the transition's reflection into the band.

The non-uniform mesh is the design variable here, so dx_profile is set by construction and the shared dead-cell primitive (uniform-grid only, issue #544) cannot run. The advisory names an rfx limitation rather than a property of this feed: the port spans the three substrate cells between the ground and patch node planes, both conductors are declared by node index, and the script asserts the realized feed node and the realized patch length on every mesh before any resonance is read off it.
